explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes venture debt as debt financing extended to early-stage companies. It is typically a form of mezzanine financing and may include warrants or conversion options that give the lender potential equity participation alongside its debt return. The Trap: Calling it debt to advanced-stage ventures is a common misreading; the workbook explicitly associates venture debt with early-stage companies, and the equity-linked features come from its mezzanine character, not from the maturity of the borrower. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook page 112, which defines venture debt as mezzanine debt to early-stage companies, possibly with warrants or conversion options.
